title: Decisions so far
summary: What the brief proposes and what this prototype currently does, kept separate on purpose.

blocks.title: Decisions so far
blocks.body: Proposal, product direction, and shipped state are different things. This page keeps them labeled.

items.title: Portable pages instead of one-off decks
items.detail: Share a link that opens without an account and presents one structured idea.

items.title: Content, widgets, and themes stay separate
items.detail: Pages are data; renderer capabilities are shared code; visual themes are token sets.

items.title: Static first release
items.detail: No database, accounts, or live collaboration in the initial product boundary.

items.title: Browse and Present shells
items.detail: The same content now runs as a scrolling page or a section-by-section presentation.

items.title: Local authoring loop
items.detail: Templates, block ordering, preview, import, and JSON export pressure-test the contract.

items.title: The product brief is sample content
items.detail: Seven generic pages let Showmob demonstrate its own structure without exposing private planning material.

columns.name: The plan locks
columns.detail: Modes named Present and Read. Author-chosen theme, viewer switching only in preview. Lifecycle: draft, preview, published.

columns.name: The prototype ships
columns.detail: Modes named Browse and Present. Viewer theme auditioning on every page. Four statuses including archived. No deploy pipeline yet - it is a hosted file.

blocks.title: Scope, kept honest
blocks.body: The repository separates the public product brief from implementation state. Git history records what changed; this page describes the current public boundary.

blocks.title: Public state record
blocks.body: This page contains product-level choices only. Private planning threads, personal attribution, and decision timestamps are intentionally omitted.

blocks.heading: Decisions belong in the open
blocks.body: Putting them inside the product is how they get stress-tested.
